root_cause_analysis.symptom: HTML generator has two redundant layers of time resolution: (1) sync-agent-data.py already injects timeline times into agent files, (2) HTML generator re-queries timeline or invents virtual times — duplicating and sometimes overriding sync's work
root_cause_analysis.root_cause: The sequential virtual time calculator was added in commit 3f51a5e BEFORE sync-agent-data.py existed. When sync was introduced (commit 13420d0), it made the HTML generator's time logic redundant but it was never cleaned up. The meal_ref timeline re-query was added in 13420d0 itself as a dual approach (sync + HTML re-query), also redundant.
root_cause_analysis.root_cause_commit_1: 3f51a5e - feat: add interactive features to Notion-style HTML generator (added sequential virtual time for attractions/entertainment)
root_cause_analysis.root_cause_commit_2: 13420d0 - feat: systematic timeline-data sync pipeline with time_hint disambiguation (added sync + meal_ref re-query in HTML)
root_cause_analysis.why_introduced: 3f51a5e needed virtual times because sync didn't exist yet. 13420d0 added sync but kept HTML re-query as belt-and-suspenders approach.
root_cause_analysis.why_problematic: Double sourcing: HTML generator overrides sync-injected times with its own timeline queries. Removes clarity about single source of truth. The sequential virtual time can produce garbage times when sync has already provided correct ones.
root_cause_analysis.proper_fix: Trust sync completely. HTML generator reads item.get('time') which was written by sync FROM timeline. No re-query needed.
